utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. No preliminaries. Therefore, the witness can be escorted in the courtroom. Mr. Lukic, you have some 25 minutes left, if I understand well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will not come as a surprise but I still remind you again that you're bound by the solemn declaration that you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Lukic will now, for another half-hour, continue his examination-in-chief. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning again, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very briefly --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 1D05497 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But before we begin with your report, I'll go back to what we finished yesterday with. You were talking about the firing tables for modified air bombs.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that people from Pretis showed you these tables, and you were asked in whose office you saw them.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where are the offices of those people in Pretis who came to your office? In which city, in which state?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their offices are in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know who was involved in the making of these tables?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Krstic yesterday. Could it be Krsmanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it was Krsmanovic. You are right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What is his first name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I said yesterday already I don't remember, but Counsel Lukic is absolutely right. The last name is Krsmanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And yesterday you referred to a certain Krstic. Who is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I got the name wrong. It is Mr. Krsmanovic, not Krstic. I made a mistake yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What is his age or what was his age at the relevant time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. But in my estimate, he could have been between 35 and 40; around 35. Never gave it any thought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Serb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was a little late with it, but if counsel can please watch the leading nature of any questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just corrected it. The Prosecution interviewed Mr. Krsmanovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So if you need more data --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Lukic, no need to comment on the questions put by Judge Fluegge. And if you think that you should refresh the memory of a witness, you should clearly announce that rather than to lead the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we move to D00240, please. At the end of the day yesterday, we talked about the case from 22 June, 1995, Cetinjska Street, 12. We saw figure 97 from the report, and now we'll just see the police report about the same incident. We need page 7 in English version and page 9 in B/C/S. In B/C/S, it's the first paragraph; and, in English, it's the third paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the police report, it says that it involves an improvised combat device based on a rocket motor, the rocket called Grad, calibre 122 millimetres, and the warhead is probably HE M107 Howitzer projectile, calibre 155 millimetres. Does this report of the Sarajevo police coincide with your findings?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, it coincides with our findings, except that we checked a certain direction of fire, and it is somewhat different to the direction of fire determined by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it's very close.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mean the direction?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I mean. It's -- our direction is very close to the one determined by the Sarajevo police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I should now like to move to an incident of 16 June 1995 in Cobanija, number 7. In English, it's on page 192; and in B/C/S, it's page 174. On that day, according to the Official Note, an air bomb exploded on the building of a thermal power station. Concerning this incident, the Prosecution tendered P933 and P1100, and Mr. Turkusic and Mr. Suljevic discussed these documents in their statements. Could we now see on the screen, figure 111 which, in English, is on page 195 and in B/C/S, 178. How far is it between the boiler room which was hit by the modified air bomb, allegedly?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't measure it, but it's approximately 20 by 20 metres, not more.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only for the record, it was entered between the boiler room, I think I said in front of the boiler room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But even how far something is in front of doesn't make sense. A distance is measured between two points, which two points did have you in mind, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not between. I said in front. That's what I was correcting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The same is true for in front. If I say in front of a building, how far is that. Or did you mean to say how far was what it was I do not know --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises. The way Mr. Lukic started the sentence, I didn't understand. He said how much space.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... how much space can we find in front of that boiler room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you mean free space or? I mean, what is space? Space is endless. I have before me 40.000 kilometres of space. Well, that's the surrounding of the earth. Could you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I didn't go that far, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that. But try to express yourself in such a way so that we understand the evidence is which are you eliciting. Do you mean space up to the next building or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What kind of space are we talking about, Ms. Subotic?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood that I was asked how much space there is outside the boiler room, limited by the building opposite on both sides. And I answered 20 by 20. That's my estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the case of a descent of a modified air bomb, where should one find the motor?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The motor is found on the point of impact, on the site of landing, and that's what we saw yesterday. In all the documentation, in all the sketches, it's at the place where the bomb hit, where the explosion occurred. Yesterday we looked at a very illustrative picture, figure 97.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the motor found in this case?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not -- not the motor and not the chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We determined that no rocket-propelled modified air bomb fell in this case because the motor wasn't found or the other components either.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Based on all the analysis you carried out, what is your conclusion regarding the precision of these modified air bombs?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My conclusion, based on our complete analysis, and that is also shown in table number 5 on page 199, is that the precision of these modified air bombs is at the level of all the systems of rocket artillery. We have a very good illustrative example for this which could be considered as experimental on such a small sample; namely, the television was targeted once and hit. It was targeted once again a month later, and it was hit again. Concerning number 13, the surveying institute which was hit, it fell, we said, 50 metres away but it's certainly not 50 metres because next to the surveying institute there is a six-lane street and one curb, so in three attempts, targeting one target at different times from different directions, the target was hit. So based on everything we analysed, I believe that this system is within the norms of all the systems of rocket artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only for the record, that table we can find on page 218 in English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I can just ask a question for clarification, Mr. Lukic. Ma'am, you said that you found -- you determined that there was no rocket-propelled modified air bomb that fell on day you went and investigated. When did you go and investigate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I didn't say that I investigated. Maybe it's a matter of interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... record what you are transcribed as having said: "We determined that no rocket propelled modified air bomb fell in this case because the motor wasn't found on -- or the other components either." Who -- who didn't find the motor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The investigating group of the CSB which provided a set of photographs from the site --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We worked with their photo documentation to make our analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have another question in follow-up. In your experience, did you ever find a modified air bomb not hitting what was targeted? Or coming to that. So a failure to ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Based on these cases that we analysed, we provided the exact distance --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was asking whether you ever came across a complete failure to hit what may have been targeted by a modified air bomb.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, two cases. One, when an air bomb hit the edge of a privately owned house and hit the ground after that obstacle and ended up in Bunicki Potok [phoen] I believe is the name where it eventually landed after that, conditionally speaking, ricochet. And another case in Cetinjska Street when it hit the edge of a building at the level of the ninth floor without reaching its target. Those are the two incidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, are they described in your report? I just don't remember.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, we discussed them yesterday -- I mean, we discussed the ninth floor incident. The other one is not in the indictment, so Counsel Lukic did not even ask me with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the ninth floor incident was a clear failure, due ricochet only or due to imprecision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We determined direction based on the impact of the explosion on the building and the direction was good. However, that position which occurred on the trajectory could not have been foreseen. I mentioned it yesterday, this building is only 15 metres higher than the target and the hit was on the ninth floor. So if you look at it from the side, it's exactly the corner of the building that was hit, so we should consider that such a obstacle could not have been foreseen by the gunner, and I would not ascribe this to imprecision because the direction was good. In other words, if that building had not been there at that altitude, the projectile would have reached the target.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The one you said is not in the indictment. Isn't it true that some of the incidents you dealt with in your reports were not in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did work with documents that are not covered by the indictment and they're all provided in the report, but we just didn't discuss them here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you explained that one of the failures that you did not deal with that because it was not in the indictment, as you said, "so Counsel Lukic did not even ask me about this." Does that mean that you have limited yourself to what Mr. Lukic asked you to look at and you didn't deal with any other incidents or experiences which might shed light on, for example, precision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if I expressed myself explicitly. We did deal with cases that are not in the indictment, and we dealt with all the cases for which we had material, and a kind of summary is given in table 6 on the following page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there may indeed have been some misunderstanding. My -- the gist of my question is: In your experience as an expert, did you ever come across modified air bombs when -- which were launched with a complete failure of reaching what was supposed to be the target? Flying wherever but not coming any close even to the intended target.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, are you asking me about my experience with this court or about my experience as a forensic expert in general? You must understand, in peacetime conditions, a forensic expert does not have experience with this kind of projectile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's -- it's your experience but not necessarily limited to any question that was asked to you in this court, and I'm focussing on modified air bombs that were launched during the armed conflict.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did not find here any bomb that was launched in all the cases that we had at our disposal, we didn't find any bomb that was launched and then behaved as a technical product with a defect that would make us think or suspect there was something wrong technically with it. And as you see in table 6, all these 16 projectiles that were launched to different extents and percentages, conform with the standards of ballistic requirements for a given system. In this system, dispersion by direction and distance is a bit higher, which is normal, because this is a rocket system, a guided one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, I'm on my feet just to thank you once again for having responded to our questions.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Ms. Subotic you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Weber. You find Mr. Weber to your right. Mr. Weber is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mirjana Andjelkovic Lukic was one of the contributors to your modified air bomb report; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: She also worked at the military technical institute; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During a certain period of time, she worked at the military technical institute, and then she continued her career at the technical experimental centre, and from there, she retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During the war, in her position at the technical centre, she worked in the specific section for the testing and verification of munitions; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You relied on her contributions as part of your report in this case; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but from a different aspect that primarily referred to the effects of bombs and how they affected space. We had a report by Mr. Zecevic that is not well argumented and not well founded, and he claimed that the spaces, the one that is affected, Ms. Andjelkovic's contribution was invaluable there because that is exactly her line of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yesterday you discussed the testing and possible existence of firing tables for modified air bombs. You even suggested at transcript page 39540 that we could get the tables through your institute. The testing you described did not happen, and these tables do not exist at your institute; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise, but it's a bit difficult for me to follow what you're saying. The tables were from 2002. Sorry, I checked that when I went back to the hotel. 2002, they do exist and they're no different to those that we discussed from the 1990s, in terms of their results and parameters that have to do with precision. They just include a larger number of projectiles.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33121 for the witness. And if we could please go to e-court page 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Coming up before you will be Ms. Andjelkovic Lukic's, your co-author's testimony from the Karadzic case. I'm going to start at line 13. Ms. Andjelkovic Lukic was asked: "Q. Doctor I am -- my question is about the testing of modified air bombs systems. I would like to you answer with a simple yes or no whether, during your period at the military technical institute and in the course of your conversations and dealings with your colleagues at the military technical institute, did you hear of testing of modified air bombs by that institute? I need a verbal response, please." Her answer was: "No, no, no, I did not, because it is certain that if I had heard about that or if that had been done, it certainly would have come to me for verification, or I would have been made aware of it. I never had that on my desk. That is a fact." Do you accept your co-author's statement on this matter as the truth?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My colleague gave you an answer and since that is what is recorded, for me that is a truthful answer. I'm sure, I assume no one wrote down anything that she had not said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: A projectile --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like my colleague to tell what kind of bombs were discussed in this instance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that perhaps may be --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because it's not the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- In re-examination a matter you wish to raise what this exactly means.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then we need the reference is from this was read from [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've given it and I think this is kind of an improper intervention.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I think Mr. Weber has given the 65 ter number and it's page 31505 from, if I understand you well, the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. As you know, we are still missing the documents. It takes some time that we get the documents when the cross starts so that's why I cannot follow. So I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's at this moment on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I mean the actual document I don't have with me so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I take it --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The transcript from Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... it's a public transcript anyhow, so if it would assist you during the next break that that even can be found on the Internet, if you want to scroll through it in the way you wish to approach it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, for the time being, I think we can proceed. Please, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: A projectile goes through a significant amount of testing before a final firing table is created; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yesterday at transcript page 39539, when you were discussing the existence of firing tables from modified air bombs, His Honour Judge Fluegge asked you: "Before the testing you saw them?" You answered: "Yes." Your testimony about the existence of firing tables for modified air bombs is not true; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Although my answer is true, the one that I provided today, the one I provided yesterday is correct as well. This is what it's all about. When a new system is being developed, any system, in order to start testing in the first place temporary firing tables have to be made. They are made on the basis of our knowledge and experience that we have from our work on previous systems. So whoever starts the testing for the first time already has a document in his or her hands called temporary firing tables. Now, whether that is the same as final firing tables that depends on everything that is written down in the meantime and possible corrections that are made on these temporary firing tables, and that is how the final product is attained. That is to say, that I had to have firing tables in my hands before any kind of initial testing so that those who do the testing can embark upon it. That's the procedure. My colleague did not say anything that was incorrect. There may have been no final testing that had reached her. The firing tables did have to exist even before any kind of initial testing is carried out on any one of the testing grounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Today, you have been confronted about the statements of your co-author and the statement that you made yesterday. This is now another version that you are coming up with; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not yet another version. We did not discuss this. I did have firing tables. My colleague would get the final testing, if that did take place. Sorry, I'm not saying that I made this. But whoever goes out for testing must have firing tables for the first projectile that would be fired during testing. Otherwise, this person would not have parameters. This is procedure, and there is nothing inconsistent there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At transcript page 39317, you were asked about the possibility of firing two shells from one 76-millimetre cannon within an interval of a couple of seconds. You answered: "Usually one minute is required, normally about one minute is required but the firings allegedly happen much faster." A 76-millimetre cannon can actually fire many more rounds per minute than you describe?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, could you quote the full answer of the witness gave yesterday before you put it to her, because I think the one-minute limit was not the only thing she said about it. Just from my recollection something about a crew.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes [Overlapping speakers] ... in all fairness to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'll paraphrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And you did give an indication that this could depend on the crew that was operating the cannon. My question to you is that a 76-millimetre cannon can actually fire more rounds per minute than you describe; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You probably read some characteristic that is there. We say that a certain weapon can follow -- can fire 1.000 bullets per minute, but when it actually happens, this does not occur. I'm sure that within a few seconds, when these two explosions occurred, two projectiles cannot be followed -- cannot be fired in succession following one another. There has to be another round of firing, charge and fire. So it's different from infantry weapons for special units. Then three projectiles are fired randomly. In this case, there is targeting, and I would not agree that somebody fired at a particular target twice within a few seconds, as witnesses have said. That is illogical.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter 33234 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: These are the firing tables for a 76-millimetre M48 B1 cannon. If we could go to page 4, the lower part of the B/C/S, and page 4 of the English translation. This is the section from the tables regarding rate of fire and we see in the top paragraph, the paragraph 12, that it does depend on the level of the training of the crew. And then we see that there's a table number 4 related to the permitted rate of fire. Directing your attention to this table, the top row appears to indicate that it's one for shooting duration in minutes; and the bottom row indicates for number of bullets per weapon. According to this chart, a 76-millimetre cannon can fire up to 25 rounds in a minute; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But look at what it says up here. That the elements have to be checked after each and every firing. Perhaps you believe that all of that is possible, but I told you, you probably found some table, and you did, indeed. So this is one minute, then 25 number of bullets per weapon; I agree with you that that is what is written there. However, if you take into account the practical situation, these are certain maximums that are being allowed for in case the barrels do not overheat and are not damaged in a more permanent way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Have you ever been deployed as part of an artillery crew operating a cannon during combat operations?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was always deployed in crews that conduct testing weapons and ammunition. If you're asking me if I was an officer ever, the answer is no. If you're asking me if I ever took part in the war, my answer is no. I don't know how else I'm to understand this question of yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 33234 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 33234 receives exhibit number P7547, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7547 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On the 29th and 30th of September, you made a number of comments about the ability to rotate the base primary charge at the base of the stabiliser, or a stabiliser, and the amount of force needed to fasten or unscrew it. At transcript page 39485, you stated: "It requires a great amount of force that cannot be exercised by hand either before or after the explosion, when it comes to trying to unscrew the tail-fin." You went on to say that based on your technical knowledge in the area: "I couldn't even think it could be just unscrewed." You also said: "A complete shell is the result of manufacturing with the base charge being screwed into the body of the stabiliser." You further explained the day before, at transcript page 39429: "When the shell is manufactured, the base charge is screwed in by using tools and a lot of force. The actual screw is lubricated by a type of cement, particular cement, which provides for further contact." These statements are not accurate; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just so I don't misunderstand your answer. When you're saying -- are you acknowledging that you've provided inaccurate statements or are you standing by the statements you previously made?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand by what I said earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For the record, the answer was yes they were accurate actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, "su" [phoen]. The answer was not "da."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic, I appreciate your assistance. At the same time, you're not supposed to tell what the answer was. But in this case, perhaps, if that's what you heard, I think there's no major objection to assisting in this way, but it shouldn't become routine. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I intervened after Ms. Subotic answered to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, it's acceptable under the present circumstances. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The fact is, is that it is nowhere near as difficult as you make it seem. Even mortar crews can insert the basic charge at the base of the stabiliser themselves; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday after my testimony, I saw a video-clip from the Krusik factory that manufactures these 120-millimetre shells and we can see exactly what the final projectile looks like and how it is tested. I saw this video-clip. I downloaded it, and I can even show it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please first answer the question that Mr. Weber put to you, whether a crew can screw a base charge on a tail-fin at the mortar -- at the position where the mortar crew is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I find this information to be totally foreign, because the stabiliser and shell is delivered in complete form with the basic charge, as I've already mentioned during my testimony, and all six charges are there, all the six additional ones and then they take them off or put them on, depending on the charge that they wish to use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so the simple answer is that you think it's not correct what Mr. Weber says that you can screw them on and off, that it cannot be done by the mortar battery crew itself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no, because there's no need to do that. It is provided delivered in completed form. Screwed on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, would you please answer the question and not a question which was not put to you. The question was not put to you whether a mortar battery crew would be in need of doing that, whether there was any reason to do it, but the question was whether they can do it. Could you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If they'd assemble it there on the ground, then probably they can do it. But then they'd have to get it in separate parts, which is absolutely impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you aware of what the mortar manuals and tables say regarding the insertion of the basic primary charge into the stabiliser?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but we can take a look at that together. I mean, I haven't read that part. I usually deal with the numerical part of tables.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33239 for the witness. Page 6 of the B/C/S and page 5 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is an excerpt from the firing tables for a 120-millimetre light mortar. Before you is paragraph 78 which addresses the handling of the shells. The section explains how the ammunition should be prepared for firing and, in the second paragraph, about three bullet points down, it states: "Opening the boxes in which fuses and powder charges are kept." And then about three additional points down from that, it states: "Pressing the basic powder charges into the spaces in the bodies of the stabilisers, if the charges are not already screwed in or positioned." Seeing this, the fact is that a mortar crew can insert and screw in the basic charge to a stabiliser themselves; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are old tables that envisaged that possibility, that is to say, for the base powder charge not to be in the stabiliser already. However, for decades how, people haven't been doing it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 33239 receives Exhibit P7548, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see that we're at the time for a possible break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the time for a break. We'll resume in 20 minutes from now. The witness may follow the usher. We'll resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, may I ask your attention for the following matter. There are still a few attestations, I take it, to be obtained by the Defence. The Defence is invited to co-ordinate with the Registry that if a presiding officer is needed for the attestation that it's better to use the presence of Registry staff and co-ordinate so that there's no need to -- for extra travel and that's more efficient and cost-saving.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We were already informed that we should gather our people in the field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And co-ordinate and discuss the matter with the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay, Ms. Subotic, I'm going to now start -- oh. Are you able to hear me?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm now --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I've put them on. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm now going to start by going over some general items with you. Did you personally author all three of the reports or did anyone else write any portions of the reports besides yourself?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just as we signed the reports, all who participated in their making are signed on them. And I mean the three reports that I discussed in the previous days were done by Mr. Poparic and I. And this part concerning air bombs were co-authored also by Mrs. Mirjana Andjelkovic Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did any of those other individuals author portions of the report besides yourself; if so, what portions?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the parts of the reports and all the stages were co-authored between us. We worked jointly on all of them. And including all the analyses. We did it all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These documents passed through several stages before they reached you, and we worked on them jointly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you, independently, reach all of the conclusions in the three reports that you have testified to?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of us individually separately came to the conclusion which we then finalised, discussing whether it's the best technical solution, and that's how it came to its final shape.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That means that you personally agreed with all of the conclusions in the report, based on your own analysis?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you personally review all of the materials referenced in the footnotes of the reports?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Last week, at transcript page 39129, you commented on a correction sheet at the outset of your testimony and stated: "We put in some corrections that we believe clarify the document." Who are you referring to when you say "we"?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My colleague Mr. Poparic and I.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How did these corrections come to your attention?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I noticed while preparing at home that it would be better, more convenient, to show it that way, and I discussed it with my colleague, Mr. Poparic, all these things that I noticed, and then we jointly made the corrections that we made.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I want now to move on to your qualifications. You are not a forensic pathologist or medical practitioner; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I see that the transcript may not have recorded my last phrase there, when I said "medical practitioner."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but at least it's now on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you not a military expert?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you understand under the term "military expert." If you mean tactician, that I am not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You are not a trained lawyer.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You are not an explosives expert?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Expert, no, but I studied them in great detail in my university.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You were employed at the military technical institute in Belgrade between 1974 and 2010; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you for the correction. You worked in the research and development department at the institute?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That entire institute deals with the research and development. I worked in the sector for classical weapons, the section of ballistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your job was to develop new weapons or improve the performance of existing weapons systems; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Conventional weapons, instead of classical.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You did not conduct any crater analyses during your 35 years of employment at the military institute in Belgrade; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the sense in which they are dealt with in this report, no. But in terms of their action and impact with a view to improvement, I certainly did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Not sure what you're saying there. A crater analysis being an analysis of a crater after an explosion, you did not do that during your 35 years of employment at the technical institute; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We analysed craters in terms of its impact and effects, not in the sense that was necessary to determine the direction of descent and parameters related to the analyses we discussed here. Have I answered your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I understand you better now. But just so we're clear, you did not conduct any forensic crater analyses?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The only crater analyses that you have attempted to forensically conduct were the ones you did in 2010 for the purpose of your reports in the Karadzic case; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You have never analysed a freshly formed crater in person; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You have never been to the scene of a mortar explosion immediately following a detonation where individuals were either killed or injured; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your CV, you list a number of reports you completed for courts in Serbia. These reports were in cases involving domestic charges for crimes like murder, involuntary manslaughter, and unlawful possession of weapons; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I said a moment ago that those cases analysed in peace time, circumstances are different to those that we are analysing here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With the exception of three cases in Serbia, the type of weapon at issue was a small-arms weapon, such as a gun or a rifle; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. In fact, I don't know whether it's with the exception of three cases. You know better at this moment because have you an overview. There are 150 findings there, after all. I don't know what's contained in them off the cuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With the exception -- sorry. None of your previous reports in Serbia relate to the use of a mortar or modified air bomb; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33116. And if we could go to page 76, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yesterday at transcript page 39479, you indicated that you took part in police investigations many times. Before you is your testimony in the Karadzic case. Starting at line 7, you were asked: "Q. Okay. It's clear from your CV and your publications that you have significant experience in the area of ballistics, but I don't see anything in your CV about any publication [sic] in the area of crime scene investigations. You haven't published in the area of crime scene investigation, have you?" Your answer: "That's not correct. That's not correct. In my CV, there are more than 100 findings which were made for courts, and in each of these I did visit the crime scene. I don't know how you missed that." Are these the investigations you took part in?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's customary in our country for the investigating judge to bring an expert to an on-site investigation, to ensure that data collection is done the best way possible. So I went out together with the investigative judge. I cannot count all the times now, but those were, many, many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just so we have a little bit more clarity, Ms. Subotic, as you might have guessed, we do have your previous reports from Serbia, you did not visit the crime scenes for each of these cases; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in each these cases. But if you looked at it carefully, wherever my findings cover reconstruction, I was there on the scene. Wherever there is an item called reconstruction and comparison of data with statements, that means I was on the scene. I cannot really give you a better answer from this position now because I cannot know at this moment how many times out of the total it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At transcript page 39191 in this case, you stated that physical evidence "is the only relevant evidence as far as my profession is concerned." You understand that physical evidence refers to tangible material objects or items; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you consider a photograph or video of an object or an area to be physical evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, I do have to consider that because I was not there on the scene. The video and photo material about effects at the target were taken into account by me as an expert as material evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Should we understand your testimony over the past week when you were discussing physical evidence that you may be referring to, then, photographs or videos?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If an explosive device such as an artillery shell or mortar round is detonated remotely - in other words, not by an impact - that is going to require, one, a secondary detonating device to be attached to the shell or round; and, two, a secondary explosive charge to cause the detonation; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There would be physical remnants at the scene of an explosion from the secondary devices attached to the shell found at or near the scene; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, yes. But with these electrical initiations, these are symbolic amounts, so they are not always found.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If things were not found, you cannot tell us that those things ever existed; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to a different topic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put one question at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, you heard two different terms: Physical evidence and material evidence. Is there any difference between the two, in your view?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this moment in this answer, I mean, the Prosecutor used the term physical evidence. When I say material evidence, I speak of the evidence from the crime scene in the documentation that I used. And physical evidence is, for instance, the stabiliser we held in our hands yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In your report, we very often came across the term physical evidence. Is that only such an artefact like we had in our hands, or is the term to be understood in a broader way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If what you say is true and I am afraid it's a matter of translation, I will check this afternoon, but I believe we used the term material evidence, not physical. I will look through my reports and I will see if it is perhaps a matter of translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Then it has to be checked because in the English translation, in the English translation of your report, I came across the term physical evidence quite frequently. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Changing topics. You are aware that the BiH MUP and internationals who investigated shell impacts used what is known as the central axis method to determine direction of fire; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The accuracy of this method determines the direction of fire within a margin of error of plus or minus 5 degrees and maybe as much as 10 degrees, depending on the area impacted and the quality of the traces on the ground; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I believe this plus/minus 10 is a very wide margin. I think the margin is smaller. Because the traces are generally very good, if there are any. But if it's earth or a very difficult surface, then you are right, the margin may be wider.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The central axis method is the best method of determining the incoming trajectory of a shell unless you have a radar system to do it; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. And I believe it exists now, it's in use and this central axis method will not need to be used any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am, I appreciate that you wanted to add stuff sometimes. If you could -- I want to move through, so if you could please listen to the question. The BiH MUP investigators did not have a better method at their disposal; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Over time, the shrapnel marks or physical traces in the ground caused by the projectile impact will erode and deteriorate; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This will make it harder to distinguish the markings from other marks on the ground; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The erosion caused by weather or human traffic affects the quality of the traces over time; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Because of these factors, it will become harder to determine the central axis and overall size of a crater over time; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If the physical traces of an impact were no longer there or were substantially altered, this would obviously impact the reliability of any measurements of these impacts over a decade later; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That depends, of course, on the damage to the remaining traces and how reliable they are. Some traces remain sufficiently reliable and can be used. But generally speaking, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The ideal time to conduct a crater analysis is immediately or shortly after the impact; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You are most likely to get the best and most reliable results when the crater is fresh; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Direction of fire should be determined by an analysis of the crater itself and not by the angles or directions of streets; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, wait a minute. Crater analysis is done based on the traces on the surface left by the explosion. However, these directions that are determined are always oriented based on direction north or some other point. We had a case when Captain Verdy determined his 17 degrees relative to direction north using as a landmark the building on Kupa when he was working on the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that the direction of fire of a projectile can be determined by the angle or directions of a street instead of the physical traces of the crater itself?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My evidence is that the direction of fire is determined based on physical traces of the crater itself and that direction has to be relative to something, relative to the central axis of the crater compared to direction north or some other fixed point.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The first time you -- the first time you went to the locations that are involved in this case was in September 2010, 15 to 18 years of a the explosions; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now, in terms of angle of descent, meaning -- what I'm referring to is the vertical angle between the flight path and the ground on impact, a minimum angle of descent can be reliably determined based on a distance to surrounding structures and buildings along an incoming trajectory; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, that is correct. However, that way you could determine the minimum angle of descent for a mortar projectile on the basis of the building that is the closest to it, and that would be, say, 42 degrees. And as far as mortar shells are concerned, there are no angles of descent of less than 50 degrees. So that is correct, but then other things have to be taken into account. So obstacles have to be taken into account. The ones that are the closest and the farthest from the point of impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: An approximate or rough estimate of the angle of descent can be made by measuring the distance between the central part of the crater and the outer peripheral traces; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the distance between the first and second crown? I don't understand what you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, for example. That would be an example of how to do that. So where the actual crater impacts its central part and the outside crowns, as you're referring to them. An estimate of the angle of descent can be made from that; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That method does exist, the one that was used by investigators of the CSB, and it primarily uses traces on the ground left by the explosion and these distances that you spoke of between the centre of the explosion and the next crown as left by shrapnel, and, of course, the dimensions of the shell, and the explosive charge or the centre of the mass that they usually used probably because they don't know exactly where the centre of the explosion was because this defect that is taken into account is the most pronounced, of course, in terms of the centre of explosion during the fall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let's just see if we understand this similarly. If the distance between the central part of the crater and the outer peripheral traces is small, then this would suggest a steeper angle of descent; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean an angle of almost 90 degrees?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No ... maybe I'll just give it you all at once and see if we understand each other. If the distance between the centre part of the crater and the outer peripheral traces is small, then this would suggest a steeper or more vertical angle of descent; where conversely if the distance between the central part of the crater and the outer peripheral traces is larger, then this would suggest a lower or less vertical angle of descent. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said to you. If the difference is small, then the angle of descent is close to 90 degrees compared to the surface and then if it is greater than it is an angle that is less than 90 degrees, depending on the distance of the second crown and what the parameters of the shell itself are, as I've already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Accurate determinations of directions of fire and angles of descent cannot be made from a viewing of a photograph alone; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that basis, the results can be checked and then the other traces that the shell left when it exploded can be assessed pretty well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Accurate determinations of directions of fire and angles of descent cannot be made from only a photograph; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not have a better choice than that, and it turned out that we were very close to accurate answers that corresponded to the measurements on the ground in the immediate aftermath. After the explosion, that is. If you remember, in each and every incident we had contrary results and this photo documentation helped us a great deal, as did the video material. Helped us establish who was closest to the actual values in view of the traces left by the shell after the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your view, can an accurate determination of direction of fire and an angle of descent be made from only a photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic is supposed not to speak aloud. Mr. Mladic, no speaking aloud any further.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Within the tolerance provided by the method itself. And you already mentioned that at the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So you would say that the -- a determination by a photograph alone would have the same margin of error as looking at the physical traces, plus or minus 5 degrees if the traces are clear in the photo, and then if they're not so clear, it's a bad photo, maybe a margin of error of 10 degrees. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to say that the photograph that was made at the moment after the explosion is equally accurate if it was made properly and then there is also personal insight on the ground. Because, do not forget, that all of these photographs were taken immediately after the incident. And that's what they're used for, so that after a while we can check and determine whether somebody did that correctly on the spot. Otherwise, there wouldn't be any photo documentation, if there weren't for this need to be able to check what an investigator did at the time, to check later, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I ask you an explanation. You were asked about the accuracy of determining a direction of fire and an angle of descent from a photograph only. And then you said - let me just take at that literally - you said: "We had no better choice, and it turned out that we were very close to accurate answers that corresponded to the measurements on the ground in the immediate aftermath." So what you're saying: Our conclusions matched with the conclusion reached at the time than explains the accuracy of our -- our ability to accurately draw conclusions from photographs. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were two questions there. First of all, you asked whether our conclusions correspond to those of the investigators. With regard to many incidents, we had contrary findings amongst the investigators themselves. For example, criminal -- do you understand what I'm saying? And on the basis of that we managed to establish what was correct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I focussed on the first part of your answer, where you said: We came to the same conclusions as those who investigated on the ground, which then, if I understood you well, was used as an argument that you could accurately draw conclusions on the basis of photographs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is correct that our results almost always coincided with some of the findings offered during the investigation. Not always but almost always, and that works in support of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What's your conclusion from that fact? Because you were asked about the accuracy of drawing conclusions from photographs. Now, what's your conclusion in relation to what you just told us, that very often your findings were in accordance, were the same or almost the same as those who did the investigation on the ground. What does that tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said a moment ago that on the basis of photographs that were made after the incident, immediately after the incident, we can carry out proper checks and we can check the measurements that were made by the investigators. Now what happened to us sometimes was that there were three or four results that were offered within the same investigation, and the photographs would help us establish who was right in terms of the traces that can be seen in the photograph, what matches that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not talking about events where there are more series of photographs but just one series of photographs. If there's a discrepancy between what you conclude and what those who did the investigation on the ground conclude, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, there are no different photographs. It is different findings that were offered to us. Photographs were one and the same. There is one photo documentation, and we had one, two, three findings in terms of measurement, in terms of positions taken. We didn't have any different photographs, different photo documentation except in one particular case. But with the same photo documentation, different interpretations were made. There are photographs there that were taken immediately after the explosion, and we found that to be extremely helpful so that we could reach conclusions on the basis of the traces that can be seen in the photo documentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, and if your conclusions are not the same as the ones who did the investigation on the ground, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We always found an explanation as to why the investigators came to an erroneous conclusion. And in different cases, there were different reasons, and we documented all of that in -- in -- in these papers of ours. I mean, I can give you any example, if necessary, but I don't think it's necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you considered that you may have made mistakes in interpreting the shrapnel pattern, for example, or the ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whenever we had a dilemma like that - and we did have such dilemmas - we made a complete overview of a particular situation. We tried to match all the information that we had. And on the basis of all of this information, in the records, in the on-site investigation, the sketch of the scene and so on, so when you put all of that together, there is a clear and unambiguous answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know? I don't have any dilemma. When somebody writes in his record, That is such and such a direction on the basis of that, and if no picture is taken that is different. However, if I take a picture ten years later and I see what it's like, then I no longer have a dilemma as to what this looked like. Because if that is what it looks like ten years later, then it was much clearer and what had been written was the opposite. Ten years before that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so no doubt at all about your own accuracy in doing this exercise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When viewing a photograph, you are limited by the distance of the camera to the object being photographed and there may be perspective issues that make it difficult to determine angles; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is why we used Google Earth, you see? We would put a street where it was and then we would reduce the negative contribution of the camera to our estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. You agree that a photograph should not be manipulated or edited in such a manner that it distorts the content of the photo; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: All of the -- what you call crater analyses that you did for your various reports were conducted either on the visits in 2010 or on the basis of photographs or video stills of the sites or some combination of those efforts; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your reports, have you included all of the photos that were taken during your visit to Sarajevo in 2010, or are there any additional photos that were not included in your report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is an entire album. It would have been too much if we included everything in this report, although it is voluminous. I regretted that yesterday; namely, why we didn't include a photograph from the Cobanija incident that was considerably clearer than the one we looked at today.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You cannot get precise measurements from a street map; correct? I'm talking about precise measurements.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, precise measurement of what?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You cannot get precise measurements based on street maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Distances of, let's say, a curb to a sidewalk, a curb to the building, the angle of a street, these types of things. A street map might give you a general idea of such distances, but they would not be precise; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The distances were not determined on the basis of town maps but directions were on the basis of Google Earth and the angles are rather precise. I mean, the direction in terms of a particular building, say, in relation to direction north. That's what I'm trying to say. We usually - not usually -- always took the distance from the sketch of the scene itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you agree that you cannot get precise measurements based on a street map?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would appreciate it if you would tell me what measurements. Certainly not crater measurements. But angles, streets, buildings in relation to direction north, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. I think everyone understands that Google Earth is satellite imagery. That's not a street map; correct? What I'm talking about is a city street map.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't know if your answer was recorded.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I'm not following. I'm saying I don't know. I mean, my answer was that I cannot determine a distance or a direction or, rather, magnitude, say the magnitude of a crater using a street map that cannot be done. However, directions, just directions of streets and buildings in relation to direction north, that can certainly be done. That is certainly not being contested.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's come up before in your testimony, but for a lot of your descriptions of the incidents or for descriptions of incidents, where you, for example, superimpose a sketch on top of a city street map and then critique the direction or what you feel to have been the direction that it should have been, why did you then not include the Google Earth image, if that's what you were using?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some were with one, there wasn't really much of a difference, some were with both. It really wasn't a special reason to use this or that. In some cases we used both. In some cases, perhaps it was more direct to use a street map, a town map, because the names of streets are there and also the names of buildings that were supposed to be recognised. Say, the wire factory we dealt with a few days ago or the TV building, then we use a city map. And sometimes we would check both. Both Google Earth and a city map and then it would always match. I mean, we did not notice that there were any mistakes made in the city maps themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I see it's almost time for a break, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'd like to start a break in one or two minutes but if this would be a suitable moment, then we'll take the break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take the break. And we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One preliminary matter was announced.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. May we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Hi, Ms. Subotic. The flight of any object through the atmosphere will are affected by, one, the velocity with which it is launched into its flight; two, the shape of the object; three, the mass of the object; and, four, the environment in which the object is flying through, including any meteorological conditions; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are other factors but I will come to it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We're going to discuss many incidents. My next question. Basic firing tables contain the adjustments that need to be made for meteorological conditions, such as air temperature, air pressure and humidity; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Firing tables also contain the adjustments that take into account other variables, such as cross-wind, headwind and tail-wind; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The difference in altitude between the firing point and the target is also relevant when making adjustments; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The adjustments in the firing tables are specifically calculated to account for the mass of a projectile, its weight distribution, and the specific aerodynamics of the specific projectile's shape; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not quite understand you -- the beginning of the question. What did you mean? Did you mean that adjustments are made by taking into account all these things you enumerated or what? I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'll just ask it without that part. The firing tables are specifically calculated to account for the mass of a projectile, its weight distribution, and the specific aerodynamics of the projectile's shape; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you make firing tables, you make them for the so-called normal mass of that projectile, which implies plus/minus one weight sign which is simply calculated, and what is understood in the -- in terms of trajectory. It's all given to -- for that normal mass. Adjustments are made also taking into account dispersion in separate tables. And it's true that according to -- or, rather, on the basis of aerodynamics which are calculated and measured, the trajectory of a projectile is determined, depending on the elements you take into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If the parameters from the firing tables are taken into account, there will be a high likelihood that the projectile will land on its intended target; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In a surface-to-surface situation, when a projectile is launched from the ground with the aim of hitting another target on the ground, the total force imparted on the projectile both vertically and horizontally will impact where the projectile lands; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just to be clear on this, provided the firing angle is the same, range depends upon the initial velocity. For example, if the initial velocity of the projectile is greater, the projectile will travel farther; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If you were firing a rocket-assisted projectile, you would need to have precise firing tables in order to fire it with any degree of accuracy; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For every projectile that is fired, you need precise firing tables. This is a rocket-assisted projectile, the one we discussed, of a type which has a very short operation of the motor compared to the total time of flight, and after that, when they reach the end of their velocity of the rocket motor they continue flying as any other projectile. And for every artillery projectile, whether rocket assisted or not, precise firing tables are needed to hit the target.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, could you seek clarification. "The one we discussed, I think we dealt with quite a few incidents where --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If I could try to clarify in the abstract.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And then see if she wants to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, when you're referring to the one we discussed, are you referring generally to modified air bombs with rockets on them?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean generally modified air bombs, because we did not cover any other rocket projectiles in this report. I'm sorry for being imprecise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I now want to talk to you about the embedding of mortar shells. 82-millimetre and 120-millimetre mortar shells do not have the same launch velocities when launched with the same number of charges; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
