utterances.text: 82-millimetre mortar shells are launched at a comparatively lower velocity with the same number of charges; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: A basis physics hypothetical here: If two objects of different mass, one four times heavier than the other, are launched with the same outbound velocity and both impact the same surface in terms of hardness, the object with the greater mass is more likely to penetrate the surface than the lighter object; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the condition they arrived to the target at the identical speed. You know, mass and velocity behave differently, depending on range.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. According to the tables, a 120-millimetre mortar shell has a total mass with fuse of between 12 kilos, 280 grams, and 12 kilos, 600 grams and this is a light mortar, depending on the type of shell and fuse. An 82-millimetre mortar shell has a total mass with fuse of between 3 kilos, 230 grams, and 3 kilos, 300 grams, also depending on the type of shell and fuse. We'll go into this more specifically but just right now, a 120-millimetre mortar shell is significantly heavier than an 82-millimetre mortar shell; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33239, page 9 of the B/C/S only. I believe this might have been admitted as P4548. Yep. And if we could to the right of this document, please have 65 ter 33098A, page 10 of the B/C/S only.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On the left, you have a table for a 120-millimetre light mortar shell for charges 4 to 6. On the right, you have a table for an 82-millimetre mortar shell for charges 4 to 6. According to the chart on the left, for the 120-millimetre shell, the firing velocity, or VO, at charge 4 is 256 metres per second; correct? I'm referring you to the top column for charge 4 or the top row.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to the chart on the right for an 82-millimetre shell, the firing velocity most similar is for charge 5 at 259 metres per second; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We also see comparatively similar velocities for the respective shells between charge 5 of the 120-millimetre shell and charge 4 of the 82-millimetre shell; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 120 with charge 5 is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness be asked to speak more slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you speak more slowly so that the interpreters can catch your words. And perhaps start your answer again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Charge 5 for the 120-millimetre shell, the contact-fuse has the initial velocity of 290 per second. And charge 5, 82-millimetre shell, has the initial velocity of 230. That shell is M4. I suppose you wanted to compare the 120-millimetre shell with charge 5 with charge 4 in an 82-millimetre shell? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Actually, no, and thank you for correcting me. The comparative -- charge 5 of the 120-millimetre shell would be similar in velocity to charge 6 of the 82-millimetre; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. With the full level of initial velocity.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I put it to you that based on its greater mass and higher outbound velocity on lower charges that a 120-millimetre mortar is more likely to embed on charge 3 or greater than an 82-millimetre mortar; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Due to its significantly lighter mass, much less explosive force would also be required to kick back a stabiliser from an 82-millimetre shell; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question? I didn't hear the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Due to its significantly lighter mass, much less explosive force - so when the mortar impacts and explodes - that -- less force would be required to push the stabiliser in a different direction or kick it back; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The force necessary to kick back a stabiliser is, first of all, defined by the dimension of the stabiliser, which is built into steel. And, otherwise, these two shells have totally different explosive charges. 120, I believe, has 2.6 kilos of explosive, and an 82-millimetre has 680 grams.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please answer the question that was put to you by Mr. Weber. Whether it's true that due to the lighter mass of the tail-fin, it requires less force to push it back, I take it, upon impact compared to the heavier 120-millimetre tail-fin. Could you answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably. Because the dimensions are smaller. But that depends primarily on the size and on the type of material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean material of what? Of the tail-fin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The material of the stabiliser. During explosion, it has to be torn off and kicked back, depending on the force acting upon it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I don't know if Judge Moloto had a question or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was just thinking that I would accept that the material would be the same, the size and weight would be different because the one is bigger than the other. But they would made from the same kind of steel, so I'm not quite sure what you mean by it depends on the material.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure the material is the same. I would have to check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 33098A into evidence at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see when you had it on the screen, didn't you say that it was already in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe the one on the left for the 120 millimetre is in evidence. There's been multiple references to the relevant pages from the 82 millimetre. There's a lot of pages uploaded in this version, and we're just tendering it all at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 33098A receives Exhibit P7549, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7549 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, turning your attention to the Vase Miskina shelling on 27 May 1992, you agree that an 82-millimetre mortar shell exploded upon impact on this occasion; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The direction of fire was 175 degrees with a margin of error; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, almost normal to the plane; that is to say, the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There direction of fire is to the south slightly to the east toward the area of Trebevic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I would really have to open it and look. I don't know it by heart. I hope you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Not at all, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, it would assist me, and perhaps my colleagues as well, if you would point us to which report we find it exactly and where approximately in that report so that we can open it and have it available for ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm referring to the shelling report, paragraph 18, which is 1D5498. And my last question went to the witness's more broad knowledge.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that direction is 175. We indicated it on the Google Earth picture and we agreed with the direction determined by the CSB investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. As part of your analysis and your discussion in your report of this incident, you rely on multiple documents from the BiH MUP investigative file, including multiple reports, death certificates and photos; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Based on your review of the investigative file, you are aware that the location where the shell impacted was in the vicinity of the school of economics; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we looked at its position at impact, taking into account the sketch of the Vase Miskina Street, 5 metres from the door, opposite the Planika facility, et cetera. We oriented it to the data given in the report and the sketch of the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. The conclusions of the investigators conflict with your opinion in this case insofar as they determined the shell came from the area of Trebevic; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, obviously they did not take into account all the elements that we had analysed, as you've seen --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... ma'am, I'm just asking to be clear. I'm just trying to define the issue that you're really taking. The conclusions of the investigators conflict with your opinion in this case, as they determined that it came from the area of Trebevic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You based your opinion for the angle of descent for the shelling of Vase Miskina on photos and your visit to the location in September of 2010; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Those photographs that we made in 2010 are in full accord with the photographs that are in the photo documentation of the CSB and that was subsequently compiled. And it is not in accord with the original photo documentation that was made when help was provided and before Vase Miskina Street was cleared. So these two documentations are not in accord with one another, and we don't know when this other documentation was made. And I already said that it was on the 10th of August that year that it was added to the case file and that that was written in hand, so we saw that on the original footage and on Robert Rogers' photographs because that was compatible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I get some clarification. Ms. Subotic, you are recorded at page 54, starting at line 2, to say: "No, those photographs that we made in 2010 are in full accord with the photographs that are in the photo documentation of the CSB, and that was subsequently compiled." And then the next sentence: "And it is not in accord with the original photo documentation that was made when help was provided and before Vase Miskina Street was cleared ..." Do I understand that there are three different sets of photographs: The photographs made by you in 2010; the photographs made by the CSB, those are in accord; and then there are photographs that were made to help which was -- when help was provided at the street.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. Your understanding is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 1D05498, English e-court page 45 only, focussing on the image. And if we could please focus on the image.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is the side-by-side comparison photograph that was discussed with you on direct examination at transcript page 39144 and shortly thereon. According to the end of the paragraph immediately above the photo - if we could please see that - the -- according to this paragraph and the caption, the photo on the left is the Roger Richards image and the one on the right from the BiH MUP investigative file from this event; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From that documentation that the investigators compiled after the clearing -- at least that is what is written there after the wounded were carried away. However, we don't know when. And then the handwritten note pertains to that photo documentation. What I said a moment ago. It said that it was on the 10th of August, 1992, that this was attached to the file.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am, please focus on my questions. I will just go step by step and it will actually go faster that way. The photo from the investigative file appears to be taken from immediately above the crater here; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Looking down at footnote 66 - and I see you have your report in front you - you specify the ERN range of the photo file and the particular ERN 00267984 for the specific photo on the right. You then state: "The distortion has been eliminated from this photograph in order to show it side by side." And you also state: "This correction did not in any way alter the facts as depicted in the photograph." My question: Did you use any computer software, Photoshop or some other sort of image editing software, on the BiH MUP photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My colleague made this compilation of two photographs, and obviously he equated the measures of the tiles on both photographs so that they could be matched.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What is the name of this colleague?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mile Poparic, the co-signatory of my report and my associate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your previous testimony in the Karadzic case, at transcript page 38362, you discussed a contemporary technology which "allows for each such photograph to be placed in a vertical position by computer analysis and thereby remove the angle from which it was filmed and deformations caused by the photography that can all be removed." Did you apply or did Mr. Poparic apply this technology to the photo from the investigative file which is before us?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I spoke about this position in terms of the orthogonal projection I said then when I testified in the Karadzic case I spoke about figure 17 and you see here that thanks to how the photograph was taken it was easy to correlate the tiles --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'd like to keep moving. If you could please focus on my question is whether or not that contemporary technology that you spoke was applied to the photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I object. My learned friend was just corrected because he was showing figure 14 and Ms. Subotic told him that they were talking about 17. So it was not right to mislead the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first then check whether it's 14 or 17 and whether it's the same in both cases or whether these are corresponding photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the paragraph -- I believe this is not correct. In the paragraph above the figure 14, it says: "In order to facilitate the analysis, figure 14 shows side by side the image of the crater taken by war correspondent Roger Richards and the image of the crater from the photo file made during the onsite investigation by the BH public prosecutor." And then the footnote after the sentence is 66 and then I'm referring to 66, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you now answer the question, Witness? Was this software applied or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was applied in the sense that the edges of the left- and the right-hand photographs were brought in line so that the craters could be compared in relation to the sidewalk, the tiles, so that it could be seen clearly that these -- that this is not one and the same crater.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you went, again, beyond the question. Apparently the software was applied. Mr. Weber then will put his next question to you, after you have confirmed, and if there's any further explanation needed, Mr. Lukic has an opportunity in re-examination. So would you please focus your answer on the questions. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we keep this photo on the screen, this image on the screen, and next to it please bring up a second photo under 65 ter 33168, page 23 of the B/C/S version only.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, coming up before you will be the BiH MUP investigative file and specifically the photo that you reference in footnote 66.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could leave it as is. Your Honours, if we could keep it as it originally appears in the photo file. It's been rotated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that how it is now? It has been rotated quite a -- couple of times. I don't know whether this is the original. Could you have -- Mr. Weber, is the way in which you would like to have it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I would have to call up now on my own computer the actual file to see if that's the -- for my purposes, I think I can make do with what's up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We see the original photo that you referenced from the photo file. This photo was taken from the side and not from above the crater; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph, yes. As far as I can remember there was a photograph that was taken in front, in that same photo documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I put it to that this photo was edited and changed in angle -- ma'am, if I could please ask my question. I put it to you that this photo was edited and changed in angle, in an attempt to create an appearance of a different crater; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course that's not correct. There are photographs that were provided here in this expert report from this same documentation that were taken from here, and here you can also see that there is no such case. So that is to say, this photograph did not need to be used. These photographs were not redacted, except that we are talking about figure 14 now. The only thing that was done there was as follows: In the photograph that is in the photo documentation, it's not the one that you showed us, the tiles, the size of the tiles was adjusted to that that was taken by war reporter Rogers in order to make a global comparison in terms of what this looks like and one can see that nothing else was done on it. Anyone who is familiar with this technology Photoshop, et cetera is aware of that. So by way of comparison, it is only that -- that the only reason why in Photoshop this was done, in terms of this photograph from the photo documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could just scroll down on the left panel. And a little bit over to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just reading in for the record on the screen before us is ERN 00267984. If we could please up just a little bit and a little bit back over to the right so the photo is back in -- centred. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time could we please take a screen capture of what's on the screen, and I tender that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This screen shot receives exhibit number P7550, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just ask you --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it the Prosecution's position that what we see on the left, which is the non-adapted photograph, that that depicts the same crater as we see on the photograph taken apparently by Roger Richards?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. It would be and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It is. I will verify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. I was misunderstanding you. I thought we were talking about the photo on the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I'm talking about is --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... the Richards photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You -- it's the position of the Prosecution that the photograph to the left which is taken without any further adaptation by software from the report which was made at the time, depicts the same crater as, if I could say so, in the more greyish photograph taken by Roger Richards, that those craters are the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If I could check one thing and then just report to the Chamber after the next break, that would be great.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. One second. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 1D5498, page 40 of the English and page 41 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: These are two figures from your shelling report related to the incident. The top figure is from the photo file in 1992 with what appears to be an annotation on it; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We could not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am, if you could please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The bottom figure contains photos that you took during your visit in 2010; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The photos you took are closer to the crater and from a different angle than the investigative file; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not close to the crater. Later on, it was zoomed in from the photograph. And then details were provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The area where the shell landed is located in a part of the city with heavy foot traffic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During your visit in 2010, you could see that the blast marks were worn down; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is why they were marked in red so that they would be preserved.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do I understand correctly that, according to figure 7 of your report, you measured the distance between the centre and the farthest edge of the crater to be 16 centimetres?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention back to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But is the top line on the centre or a few inches -- a distance away from the centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand what you mean. I'm sorry. The measuring was carried out between the 24th and the 40th centimetre. That was our assessment, I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question had been whether the 16 centimetre distance starts from the centre of the crater. I assume that the centre of the crater is that white dot in the centre where your measuring ruler stands and I'm saying is it really from the centre or is it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. The photograph with the scale is a photograph from the photo documentation of the Bosnian investigators with the 16 centimetres marked red from the edge of the crater to the edge of the tile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So it's not from the centre of the crater. That explains it. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. The very edge of the crater to the tile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention now to the top photo, you agree that the blast marks from the crater extend beyond 16 centimetres; right? The farthest blast marks?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, your question has not been transcribed fully, and as a result I can't remember it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I will repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I was directing your attention back to the top photograph and asking if you agreed that the blast marks from the crater extend beyond 16 centimetres? The top photo. You agree; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think your question was a little bit problematic, Mr. Weber. We were told the 16 centimetres indicate the distance between the line between the blocks on the footpath and the edge -- it's not from the centre of the crater, as the witness responded to Judge Moloto. And, therefore, perhaps you should rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps would it assist if we have the title that we could read the title of figure 7 in English version. That's on the next page. So that we know what is depicted in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We are, at the moment dealing with figure 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 6. Okay. Then we'll leave it to figure 6 at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let's keep moving along. Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 331 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should put the question in the correct form again with respect to figure 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So what I'm asking you generally - and we do see that there's some measurements that you annotated on here - is whether based on this photo, you would agree that from the centre of that crater, as marked by that white dot to the external peripheral outer traces, that that is more than 16 centimetres?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not the edge of the crater. That is a different effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I understand you're saying that. What I'm asking you is that distance is more than 16 centimetres; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You see that the investigators marked it with chalk. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33168, page 5 of the B/C/S and page 3 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, are we at the beginning of a longer exercise --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then perhaps it's better to -- to take the break first. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes, Ms. Subotic. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at 25 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can report back on -- as I indicated last session with regards -- this is with respect to the Richards photo, what's been called that. In the report, it's not really clear to us what the source of the photograph is. We have independently checked the available information from the institute for genocide and according to the online photo gallery, it does indicate it from Mr. Richards. However, it does not include information on the location of the crater or the site being depicted. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not what we asked for. We asked whether the position of the Prosecution is that it's the same; yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Based on that, which is why I'm saying that, the Prosecution is not able to agree that is the same crater that is being depicted in the Richards photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's proceed. And I think that's exactly what the report tells us, that it's not the same crater. Apart from whatever else may have been written there, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I've reported what the known information is and I'm happy to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, before you is the first full document in the investigative file for the Vase Miskina Street shelling. It's the official report of the incident dated 30 May 1992. We could not locate reference to this document in the footnotes of your report. Could the Prosecution please have the next page of the English translation, e-court page 4. And if, for the witness, we could please enlarge the lower portion of the page before her. So I believe we are seeking page 5 of the B/C/S, lower half and page 4 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: English page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We have the correct pages. If we could please zoom in the middle section of the B/C/S version so it is a little bit more visible for her. And if we could -- it's going to the second full paragraph down in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, toward the bottom half of the page before you, the report states: "The shell made a 50 by 60 centimetre elliptic-shaped crater on the concrete sidewalk with peripheral traces of 60 to 100 centimetres away from the centre of the crater and arranged in an arc around it." The peripheral traces measured in May 1992 indicate that the distance from the centre of the crater to the peripheral traces was at least 40 centimetres; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. And we quoted this in our report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Based on these measurements, I put it to you the actual angle of descent was much lower than the 83 degrees you arrived at.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of these measurements, yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 10 of the B/C/S and page 80 [sic] of the English translation. I'm looking for page 8 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Last week at transcript page 39136, you stated regarding this incident: "First of all, there is no police report from an on-site investigation which was conducted at the time of the evacuation." Before you is the 27 May on-site investigation report related to the Vase Miskina shelling. According to the document, an on-site investigation was carried out under the supervision of an investigating judge on the same day of the shelling, 27 May 1992, at 1400 hours. The ballistics findings are in the same document. You agree that there was an on-site investigation on the same day of the shelling; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said that, I meant there was no special police on-site investigation. As for this investigation that was carried out with the investigating judge, we know about that, and it was quoted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time, the Prosecution would tender the complete BiH MUP investigative file for the Vase Miskina file under 65 ter 33186. I believe a number was already reserved for it as D1243 MFI and this was at transcript page 39142.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, that is the complete report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The problem, it's obviously recently uploaded a couple of days ago so we really have to go through the same and we are checking when, actually, it was uploaded into the system. So.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... most of this document has never been given to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has it not been disclosed? That's apparently what you are telling us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to our records, copies of this material and files were disclosed in the Karadzic case on 2 February 2010 and also in the Mladic case on 24 February 2012.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In addition, the witness said she quoted, she had it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: She didn't see this whole document. I'm talking about the whole document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's been disclosed and if portions of this had been used by your expert, Mr. Lukic, then I take it that you have -- is the only issue that you do not know whether this is the complete report or is it there anything else? Is there any other reason why it should not be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I know that I have never seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that's not relevant, whether you or --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I thought I saw everything they saw and we are trying to locate it in EDS system, it's not there. So it is not disclosed to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So your conclusion then is that it would have not have been disclosed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I'm happy to assist Mr. Lukic. I know there are multiple ERNs related to this file. So what I quoted from were copies of this, and I do have an ERN range I can give to Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Microphone. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't understand whether we received more documents and now it's compiled or whether everything was disclosed to us before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently if the witness says that she referred to it, then it comes a bit as a surprise that the Defence is totally unaware because this is evidence you are presenting before this Chamber. Give me one second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may add ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problems potentially remaining, Mr. Lukic, is because you used the -- at least portions of this document as well, there are two issues remaining. The one is whether it was never disclosed. Then, still, you apparently were aware of portions of it. The second issue is whether this now is the complete document, yes or no. We'll admit it into evidence. You have one week to revisit one of these questions if there's any reason to do so. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The reserved number for the document is D1243, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence and the Defence has one week to revisit the issues I specifically raised. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, just to assist the Defence, because I think that there are multiple ranges that the file has been restamped. We were showing ERN range 02179616 to 02180115 was disclosed in February 2012 in disclosure batch 5 and then redisclosed again on 20 July 2012 in disclosure batch 5.2. If that's assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, if you would read the transcript, it says it was "slowed." Well, perhaps you said that it was disclosed, but perhaps slowing down was the real thing that needed your attention at this very moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. At this time the Prosecution also tenders the original video footage related to the shelling under 65 ter 33096A. Ms. Subotic relies on footage from the shelling as part of her report and this is the better quality video we referenced at transcript page 39140.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 33096A receives Exhibit P7551 Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I see that Ms. Stewart is offering the copies on CD. Therefore, P7551 can be admitted and hereby is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, you are aware that Mount Trebevic is a significant elevation to the south of Sarajevo; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 1D05498, page 50 of the English and page 51 of the B/C/S. And if we could focus on table 5 -- I believe table 4. In paragraph 15 of your report, where you are discussing the Vase Miskina shelling, you include table 4 with ranges for different 82-millimetre shells. Could you please first confirm that these ranges are taken from the 82-millimetre mortar table you reference in footnote 82?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You did not factor the elevation of Mount Trebevic into these ranges; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the tables were made for 500 metres, but, no, I did not -- well, I had to do it directly. I'd have to check. I mean, plus 500 is the standard way of doing these tables. At least over the past 20 years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think there may be some misunderstanding. Mr. Weber, you may have not been very precise, but what you wanted to refer to, I take it, is the difference in elevation rather than at what standard elevation you would test these projectiles. Did you, when you used this table, did you consider that there is a difference in altitude for possible places of firing and places of impact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- this is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have not considered that. That is an answer to my question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And Your Honour thank you for the clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now for 82-millimetre M74, you list the ranges for the primary charge through charge 4 and nothing for charges 5 and 6. Later in the paragraph, you state that an 82-millimetre M74 fired with charge 6 could have been fired from the territory controlled by the VRS. Based on the tables the information you have for the M74 does not appear to be incorporated into table 4 of your report. Do you agree that we should rely on the actual tables which do indicate that an M74 has the range you describe later in your report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't think it was necessary for me to mention the other two either because this has to do with the stabiliser that was found far away. I mean, it doesn't even -- people don't even know where it was found and no attempt was made for it to be in the surface at the place where the explosion took place. That is to say, that no way more than charge 4 could have been used.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: An M68 82-millimetre mortar is a practice round; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so but we can look. I don't think so because these are data for M68, M1. We can look at the tables.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I want -- the Chamber actually now has them in evidence. If we could have 65 ter -- I'm sorry, it's just been admitted. Exhibit P7549. And if we could go to page 34 of the B/C/S and page 59 of the English. Could we actually go one page further in the B/C/S. But I believe we can leave the same translated page up. And if we could still go one further, to the end of charge 6 is what I'm looking for. If we could go on. And one more further. Thank you. Thanks for your patience. I'm sorry. We're almost there. One page further. Here we go. Thank you very much. In paragraph 16 of your shelling report, you indicate that the maximum range of an 82-millimetre M74 is 4850 metres. Before you is a page of the firing tables for this type of mortar, and if I direct your attention down to the very last line of it, is it correct that you based the maximum range on the last entry from this page of the table?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't see where the problem is. But this has nothing to do with what you asked a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wait for the next question, please, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 13 of the B/C/S and page 17 of the translation. And, I apologise, I have some wrong paginations here. If we could go forward six pages in the B/C/S. And if we could please go ... I'm looking for the ERN that ends in 4842, so I believe it's now three pages back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's not 42 at the end. There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: All right. Based upon this page of the table, the maximum range for an 82-millimetre M74 mortar fired on charge 2 is 2180 metres; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it doesn't have an angle of descent of 82 to 84 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The angle of descent in this table is indicated for that weapon with that charge as 83 to 84 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Consistent with the findings of the BiH investigators, Serb military forces in the area of Sarajevo were firing shells on 27 May 1992 from the direction of Trebevic; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I want to show you something --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at an exhibit. Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 17610 for the witness. This is an intercepted conversation involving Milisav Gagovic from 27 May 1992. Colonel Gagovic was the acting commander of the JNA 4th Corps in May 1992. He -- during the conversation he's speaking with a Colonel Cado, who states: "People have just told me that a shell coming from the direction of Trebevic fell down near the faculty of economics and killed five people." "Gagovic: From Trebevic? "Cado: Yes, somewhere from that direction. "Gagovic: Who the fuck is firing from up there constantly." Seeing this, I put it to that you the fact is that Serb forces were aware of the firing from Trebevic on that day and fired in the vicinity of the Vase Miskina shelling referenced here as the faculty of economics. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Maybe you can assert that on of the basis of this, but I don't have that choice unfortunately. I have to show evidence and I must have all the evidence consistent with each other in order to determine a direction of fire. I would maybe have -- like to have the same degree of liberty as you do, but I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 17610 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar -- Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We always object to these intercepts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's the standard objection and that objection is denied. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 17610 receives Exhibit P7552, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7552 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, we just have a couple of remaining moments, so I'll just try to cover some general questions before the end of the day. If multiple projectiles were fired at the same location within a period of time of not more than 15 minutes, do you agree that this shows that the location is being intentionally targeted?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be logical to conclude that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. If multiple projectiles were fired into the same half-kilometre area over the course of four to six hours, do you agree that the intention is to target that area?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you said, I'm not a military expert. I don't want to interfere into tactics. Let's say that I would try to get away from that area. I cannot give you a qualified answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's why I was asking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Mr. Weber, the Chamber, at various moments, has made observations as to what are the limits of the expertise of this witness, and I would like you to keep in mind those limits as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honours. I appreciate your indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And actually, Your Honours, I'm about to start into a large different area. I know it's a couple of minutes early --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps better not to interrupt if it is -- unless you would have one or two small questions, but if not. It's of some concern anyhow, Mr. Weber, that you don't have a few small questions, but then perhaps it's better to adjourn for the day. Ms. Subotic, same instruction applies as I gave the previous days. We adjourn for the day. Since we are not sitting on Fridays, we'll adjourn until Monday, the 5th of October, 9.30 in this same Courtroom I, and you, again, hereby are instructed not to communicate with whomever about your testimony, either given or still to be given. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, you're supposed not to speak aloud. If you want to bring anything to the attention -- and you have been communicating the whole of the morning with the public gallery which you are supposed not to do, so please refrain from doing it. Focus on what happens here rather than on the public gallery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: However, before we really adjourn --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, if you want to in any way address the Chamber, you can do so through counsel. Mr. Stojanovic, if there's really anything then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, your behaviour is fully contrary to what you're expected to do, and that's already the whole of the morning. Mr. Stojanovic, anything to be addressed at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, Your Honour. What Mr. Mladic was trying to protest is that his request to have a visit today was rejected, and he is protesting because the Detention Unit did not allow that visit. That's all. Nothing else that is not connected with the goings-on in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you know exactly how to deal with any request which is denied and how to approach that. And you also know that the Trial Chamber is not involved in such matters and Mr. Mladic is apparently insistent on his bad behaviour. We leave it to that. But I would -- I would like to briefly deal with a matter before we adjourn in private session. Could we turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume Monday, the 5th of October, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.
